messages:
maya: Saw a correctness blip in canary: soft-demote allowed a new owner to serve reads before prefill; client observed stale read after a recent write.

peter: Can you paste logs?

maya: Short extract:
```
[2026-05-11T11:02:01Z] write prefix=cust9/session k=s1 -> ok seq=772
[2026-05-11T11:02:02Z] soft-demote prefix=cust9/session token=stk:9
[2026-05-11T11:02:02Z] handoff accepted token=stk:9
[2026-05-11T11:02:02Z] read k=s1 -> value=old (stale)
```

qiao: Soft-demote was supposed to be safe because we mark prefix warming and forward reads. Looks like warming flag wasn't respected on some read fast-path.

maya: Exactly. It hit the in-memory cache lookup that doesn't consult warming state when under high concurrency.

peter: Two axes: (A) fix fast-path to check warming state, cost extra branch; (B) enrich token so new owner refuses to serve keys below token.last_seq until it has caught up. The token approach avoids touching hot-read fast path for steady-state.

qiao: Token needs to be durable on old owner. If last_seq is only in-memory we still lose. So either force small durable checkpoint on demote or attach a signed WAL-offset marker.

maya: I lean token+marker. On demote: write tiny checkpoint {prefix, last_seq, wal_off} to local meta-store (cheap append), sign into token. New owner waits for local wal_off >= marker before clearing warming.

peter: Complement with a quick safety check: on a first local cache miss during warming, do a one-shot delta fetch from sequencer for ops > last_seq. That avoids long forward windows and only adds cost once per prefix handoff.

qiao: We must be careful about GC/compaction: wal_off might wrap or be compacted. Use monotonically increasing demote_id instead and keep small retention of mappings to wal_off for demote windows.

maya: Good point. Also add telemetry: warming-hit-rate, token-blocked-reads, demote-checkpoint-latency. Gate under ff.

ops-bot: Created ticket RM-6622: "soft-demote-token-checkpoint-and-warming-fix" assigned to peter & qiao. :white_check_mark:

maya: I'll open a short RFC with the token format and perf targets. Thanks.
